The 2D engine moves from XFoil 6.97 to XFoil 6.99.

This is a development pre-release. Project files and command-line options may still change.

## What changed

* **XFoil 6.99 engine.** 6.99's wake point count, and the surface-integrated pressure drag CDp instead of CD − CDf. The integral boundary-layer correlations and their calibration are unchanged.
* **New analysis controls.** Separate top and bottom Ncrit, the wake length behind the trailing edge, and the wake dissipation constant. They are available in Studio, on the command line (`--ncrit-bot`, `--wake-length`, `--wake-dissipation`), and in XFoil scripts (`VPAR NT`, `NB`, `WAKE`, and a three-value `LAG`).
* **6.99 file formats.**
  * Polar files carry two Ncrit values and the transition panel index of each side (`Top_Itr`, `Bot_Itr`).
  * `DUMP`, `DMP` (24 columns) and the polar listings follow 6.99.
  * Older single-Ncrit files still read.
* **6.99 commands.** `GDES NMOV` (offset the contour along its normal), `CAMB WRTT` (thickness and slope), and `VPLO XPLO` (boundary layer against arc length, also in Studio).
* **Checked against MIT XFoil 6.99.**
  * Six committed 6.99 polars match at their printed precision.
  * The raw-array audit's new-control cases agree with the double-precision Fortran within 1e-7 of each quantity's scale.
  * The full audit is not bit-identical; [docs/xfoil-6.99.md](https://github.com/notmanan0/Foiley/blob/master/docs/xfoil-6.99.md) lists the remaining differences.

## Compatibility

* Projects are saved in format 3. Projects from v0.1.0-dev.1 open unchanged, but v0.1.0-dev.1 cannot open format 3 projects.
* Polars computed with v0.1.0-dev.1 keep their 6.97 values. 6.97 CDp is CD − CDf; 6.99 CDp is integrated over the surface, and the two are not interchangeable.
* New 6.99 polars join the same 3D polar family as the existing ones when Mach, Ncrit and trips agree. Only a different bottom Ncrit forms a separate family.
* Importing a 6.99 polar file that has no `CDf` column records friction drag as 0 (unknown) instead of computing CD − CDp.
